title: Solving the Poisson equation using coupled Markov chains

split.decision: Independent materialized initial-state observations; val/test each retain 1000 runs. Generation seeds and exact estimand are excluded from inputs.

baseline.paper_ref: Historical source inefficiency 179489396019.827; no new full reference has been run.

allowed_changes: Unbiased estimation constructions, couplings exposed by the fixed oracle, reservoir/tuning choices, auxiliary regressions or control variates and numerical methods may change.
UPAVE k/L/m/R values are baseline computation choices; an auxiliary loss cannot alter P, h or v(P,h).
When retaining the supplied reservoir UPAVE routine, changing only k=500, L=500, m=2500, R=50 or x_0=0 does not count as a method improvement.
fixed_contract: Estimate the asymptotic variance v(P,h) of the fixed AR(1) Markov kernel using counted transitions, minimizing estimator variance times transition cost.
P is the specified AR(1) kernel with coefficient .99, h(x)=x, initial law N(0,16), supplied independent initial states and the frozen single/coupled callback oracle.
The unbiased asymptotic-variance estimand, 1000 independent runs, sample variance, actual single+2*coupled transition cost and 3-SE mean guard remain fixed.
Supplied data/splits, evaluation metric, trusted evaluator and lawful information access.
method_freedom_review.budget_policy: agent overall deadline; separate overall formal replay budget
forbidden_substitutions: Do not substitute another Markov kernel/stationary distribution, use the analytic answer as a constant, bypass callback simulation, forge cost or share runs.
No altered initial observations, hidden seeds or changed transition-cost accounting.
Training or fitting reusable model state or learned preprocessing on validation features or labels, including final train+val refits or validation-based distillation.
Using closed-form results specific to this AR(1) kernel, such as its analytic Poisson solution or stationary moments, in place of estimation does not count as a method improvement.
